sources.title: PhonePe consumer payments and financial services
sources.supports: Positions the consumer app around transfers, recharges, bills and financial services for Indians broadly; distinguishes consumer and business offerings.

sources.title: Rural merchant expansion plans, 24 September 2026
sources.supports: Explicitly targets rural merchants and villages for payment-device deployment, onboarding and support; this is merchant positioning, not the demographic composition of consumer-app users.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday payments for people sending money, shopping, recharging phones and paying bills, alongside access to other financial services.

secondary.label: Rural merchants
secondary.text: PhonePe has a specific expansion programme for small merchants in villages and rural areas, including payment devices and onboarding support. This concerns its merchant network.

notes: Tier 2+ registered-user figures are not used as a rural classification.

sources.title: Google Pay India: everyday payments
sources.supports: Markets family transfers, payments to friends and neighbourhood shops, online shopping, recharges and bills as general everyday uses.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday payments for sending money to family and friends, paying shops, recharging phones and settling bills across India.

secondary.label: Teenagers
secondary.text: A separate under-18 experience lets teenagers make core payments with additional safeguards and restricted content. Users can move to the full experience at 18.

notes: The teen experience is a secondary audience and does not define the main app.

sources.title: Paytm consumer payments and business services
sources.supports: Markets transfers, shopping payments, recharges and bills broadly; separately advertises merchant acceptance tools and the Paytm for Business app.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday payments for sending money, paying in shops or online, recharging phones and managing household bills.

secondary.label: Teenagers & parents
secondary.text: Pocket Money is a supervised payment feature for teenagers, with parents or trusted family members managing spending access and limits.

secondary.label: Merchants
secondary.text: Paytm for Business separately serves merchants accepting online and in-store payments through QR codes, Soundbox and other payment tools.

notes: Teen positioning refers to Pocket Money; it does not resolve the separate 18+ wording in general platform terms.

sources.title: super.money: payments and financial products
sources.supports: Describes a general payments app for transfers and merchant scan-and-pay, with cashback, cards, deposits and loans.

sources.title: About super.money
sources.supports: Explains a focus on helping young Indians access financial products while stating a broader mission of access to money and credit for every Indian.

sources.title: super.money co-founder on youth-focused marketing, 17 September 2025
sources.supports: Interview describes a marketing focus on Gen Z and millennial consumers, specifically including first-jobbers in their mid-twenties.

primary.label: Young adults & first-jobbers
primary.text: Everyday UPI and cashback with a marketing focus on young Indians and people starting their first jobs.

notes: No minor audience is inferred from Gen Z branding.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: A general UPI app for transfers to friends and family, shop payments, bills and other everyday spending.

sources.title: FamApp by Trio: developer app description
sources.publisher: Tri O Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd / Google Play
sources.supports: Developer description updated 5 November 2026 covers bank-linked UPI, wallet, card and savings tools; explicitly describes money management as suitable for any age group and also addresses a digital generation.

sources.title: Teen payment apps and FamApp, 13 June 2026
sources.supports: Describes FamApp as an early platform targeting teenagers directly, with prepaid-card spending and parental supervision; this substantiates teen positioning rather than inferring minors from Gen Z.

primary.label: Teens & young adults
primary.text: Payments and money-management tools with a long-standing teen audience and a focus on the next generation. FamApp now also markets its services across age groups.

notes: Youth emphasis is an editorial synthesis of current next-generation branding and documented teen positioning. Current developer copy is broader; no numerical age band or teen-only access is asserted.

sources.title: WhatsApp Payments in India
sources.supports: Markets bank-to-bank payments within chats for sending money home, sharing gift costs and repaying friends; describes transfers with users of UPI-based apps.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: People who want to send and receive money inside their everyday chats, including family transfers and shared expenses with friends.

primary.label: Credit cardholders
primary.text: Credit-card users who want bill payments, spending tracking and membership rewards in one app. Its core positioning centres on timely card repayments and member benefits.

notes: Credit-score-based membership does not establish a particular income, gender or urban demographic.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday payments for shopping, recharges, household bills and travel, using Amazon Pay UPI or wallet services.

sources.title: MobiKwik payments and financial services
sources.supports: Describes UPI and prepaid-wallet payments for shopping, transfers, recharges and bills; distinguishes consumer services from business acceptance products.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday UPI and wallet payments for shopping, transfers, recharges and bills, with additional financial services.

secondary.label: Rural & first-time users
secondary.text: Its financial-inclusion approach makes first-time users, including people in rural communities, a useful secondary audience.

secondary.label: Small merchants
secondary.text: Separate payment-acceptance services address kirana stores, street vendors and online sellers. The offline merchant strategy also targets Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

notes: The rural audience is an interpretation of the stated inclusion strategy and qualitative customer description, not a measured rural share.

sources.title: About Groww: simple investing
sources.supports: Positions investing around ease, speed and transparency, with mutual-fund SIPs, stocks and advanced trading products.

primary.label: Young & first-time investors
primary.text: Simple investing tools for people getting started, especially younger adults. Experienced investors and traders can also use Groww. This audience refers to its investing platform.

notes: Investor-age and city-tier profiles describe Groww investment users, not Groww Pay-only users. They do not establish an exclusive age target, a rural classification or a women-only audience.

sources.title: Moneyview: personal finance products
sources.supports: Describes accessible financial services broadly, including loans, digital gold, fixed deposits, insurance, cards, credit tracking and UPI payments.

primary.label: Salaried & self-employed borrowers
primary.text: Personal loans for salaried and self-employed applicants are a central offering. The app also provides payments and other financial services.

notes: Personal-loan user demographics and underwriting criteria are not applied to all app or UPI users.

sources.title: INDmoney: trading, investing and money management
sources.supports: Markets investment access across Indian, US and global markets, plus consolidated investment, net-worth and family-account tracking.

primary.label: Investors
primary.text: People investing in Indian and US markets and managing their overall finances. It combines investment products with net-worth and family-account tracking.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday prepaid payments for individuals, including people without a traditional bank account. Customers can use a personal UPI handle, RuPay card and bill-payment tools.

secondary.label: Merchants
secondary.text: Digi Vyapaar is a separate offering for merchants using Digi Khata's business services.

secondary.label: Kiosk agents
secondary.text: Digi Kiosk partners help customers open prepaid accounts and access assisted payment services. This is an agent role rather than the individual wallet audience.

notes: This is Pay Point's Indian prepaid-account product, not the similarly named Pakistani bookkeeping app. No rural demographic is inferred from kiosk distribution.

sources.title: ABCD app: payments and financial services
sources.supports: Presents ABCD as an app for financial needs across loans, investments, insurance and payments, with financial tools and guidance.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: People managing payments, borrowing, investments and insurance through the ABCD app. Its all-in-one financial-service positioning covers a range of everyday money needs.

sources.title: Shriram One and the urban-rural digital divide, 5 March 2026
sources.supports: Company release explicitly positions the app for urban and rural use, describing rural and semi-urban accessibility through simple design and local language. It is company marketing, not independent user measurement.

primary.label: Broad audience · rural focus
primary.text: Payments and financial products for urban and rural customers, with a particular focus on making the app accessible in rural and semi-urban areas.

secondary.label: Salaried & self-employed borrowers
secondary.text: The loan services include personal loans for salaried applicants and business loans for self-employed applicants. These are borrowing audiences within the wider app.

sources.title: About Jar: saving habits and digital gold
sources.supports: Positions digital-gold saving as accessible to Indians broadly, with a mission to make saving simple and turn it into a daily habit.

sources.title: Jar investment thesis and intended savings market
sources.supports: Jar investor describes its savings platform for middle-India households and a specific opportunity helping young Indians begin saving and investing. Historical user percentages are not treated as current measurements.

primary.label: First-time savers · youth focus
primary.text: Small, regular gold savings aimed at people beginning to save, with a particular focus on young Indians.

notes: The youth positioning is supported by the investor's stated market thesis. No numerical age band, rural audience or gender is inferred from saving amounts or smaller-city adoption.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday payments for Tata Neu users, including sending money, paying shops and settling bills.

notes: The researched product is Tata Pay within Tata Neu; general shopping and payment uses do not establish an affluent or urban-only audience.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Consumer wallets for everyday payments and transfers, including people using an employer or partner payment programme.

secondary.label: Businesses & service providers
secondary.text: The separate platform offering serves businesses and service providers launching payment services and branded wallet programmes. These organisations supply programmes to consumers.

notes: Provider-level business marketing is kept separate from the consumer-wallet audience. Programme availability varies, and parts of the consumer FAQ are dated.

primary.label: Savers & investors
primary.text: People who want liquid-mutual-fund investing alongside everyday UPI payments. Its central use is keeping money invested and redeeming units when a payment is made.

notes: This is investment-linked payment positioning, not a guaranteed-interest bank account or evidence of a particular income group.

primary.label: Women
primary.text: Women who want to invest, make payments and build confidence managing money. Financial learning and community support are part of the same women-focused positioning.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Everyday wallet users making shop payments, recharges, bill payments and domestic money transfers.

notes: This audience refers to the domestic wallet; current wallet terms use Wizzpay/Wizzmoni names. Unimoni's separate foreign-exchange and remittance businesses do not establish the wallet's audience.

primary.label: Students, early earners & freelancers
primary.text: FD-backed cards aimed at students, people starting work, freelancers and gig workers who are building a credit history. The app also offers everyday UPI payments.

notes: The main positioning is access to credit cards and payments, rather than a general investment platform. No age band is inferred from early-earner or student labels.

primary.label: Broad audience
primary.text: Prepaid wallet and card users managing day-to-day payments through QuikWallet and related programmes. The consumer app combines spending tools with card controls.

secondary.label: Students
secondary.text: Student-card offerings are specific partner prepaid programmes within LivQuik's wider product range.

secondary.label: Older adults
secondary.text: Senior-focused partner programmes include Khyaal cards and other elderly-card offerings. This audience is specific to those programmes.

secondary.label: Businesses
secondary.text: Businesses and programme partners can issue and manage prepaid cards, including cards for employee expenses. This is separate from the individual cardholder audience.

notes: Partner student and senior programmes do not describe every QuikWallet user. Student cards are not automatically classified as services for minors.
